system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: In the CoRE system, the interpreter constructs a detailed prompt with four elements:
system_prompt_style.note: The prompt is assembled per step from four parts: task description, current progress, retrieved observation and current instruction. The observation part is not included in every step. This is paper-only; the CoRE repo code was not in the bundle.

env_context_strategy.note: The paper describes memory retrieval of tool observations only. The bundle has no CoRE task template or tool list.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Current Progress: Summarizes the previous steps including what has been done or decided, helping maintain a narrative flow.
context_compaction.note: Intermediate results are also kept in temporary memory and only relevant ones are retrieved. This is paper prose only.

observation_format.note: The paper mentions that some OpenAGI observations are images. The bundle has no CoRE observation-conversion code.

tool_call_format.note: The paper says tool name and arguments are decided from the LLM output (Sec. 3.2.3) but gives no parser syntax. The CoRE parser is not in the bundle.

tool_count.note: The CoRE tool registry is not in the bundle. The AIOS rust tool.rs is only a placeholder.

edit_primitive.note: The CoRE tool registry is not in the bundle.

tool_schema_source.note: The CoRE tool schema code is not in the bundle.

protocol_standardization.note: The AIOS README mentions an MCP Server for computer-use. That belongs to the AIOS kernel, not to the CoRE interpreter code, which is absent.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: the system executes a single step in four procedures.
loop_primitives.note: A human-written step program drives execution. Each step runs a fixed sequence: retrieve, build prompt, optionally call a tool, then branch. There is also react-like tool use within a step.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: For each step in the program, the above four components are separated by “:::”
planning_granularity.note: The plan is a human-authored CoRE program with steps, types and connections, followed by the interpreter.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: we propose the CoRE system, which utilizes Large Language Model (LLM) as an interpreter to interpret and execute instructions step-by-step.
multi_agent_topology.note: This rests on paper prose only.

delegation_mechanism.note: The evidence is paper-only; there is no agent factory for CoRE.

human_in_loop.note: The CoRE run loop is not in the bundle.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: The system’s memory serves as a repository of all prior observations related to the program
short_term_state.note: State consists of the observation memory, the current step pointer and the progress summary. This is paper prose only.

long_term_memory.note: The paper memory is temporary and within a run. CoRE code is absent.

self_verification.note: The LLM evaluates results only to choose the next branch (Sec. 3.2.4). That is not verification.

rollback.note: The AIOS terminal rollback belongs to LSFS, not CoRE.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: Terminal: Similar to the “end” or “return” statement, this step marks the conclusion of the program
termination_condition.note: This is the closest value: the run ends at a program-defined terminal step reached by LLM branching.

execution_isolation.note: The CoRE workspace code is absent. AIOS runs agents in a ThreadPoolExecutor, which is not CoRE.

eval_hooks.note: The paper evaluates on OpenAGI, but the bundle shows no evaluation runner.

target_domain.evidence_quote: we employ our proposed system for agent task solving based on natural language programs
target_domain.note: The system targets natural-language programming of tool-using agents.

open_source.evidence_quote: This work is open-source at https://github.com/agiresearch/CoRE
open_source.note: The LICENSE file content is not in the bundle.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: We conduct experiments on both closed-source and open-source LLMs:
model_agnostic.note: The paper uses GPT-4 and Mixtral. AIOS supports many backends.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: This work is open-source at https://github.com/agiresearch/CoRE
primary_artifact.note: The bundled repo is the AIOS kernel, not the CoRE interpreter, so the coding relies on the paper.

first_release_date.note: No CoRE tag or v1 date is in the evidence. Only v2 (21 May 2024) is shown.

pinned_version.note: The pin is for the AIOS repo, not agiresearch/core. The full hash is not given.

stars.note: The count is for the AIOS repo; there is no stars count for agiresearch/core, and no date stamp is given.
